source.title: Driving the Wrong Way: Leveraging Interpretability in End2End Autonomous Driving Models

record.tranche_reason: The study uses sparse autoencoders to obtain interpretable feature directions and analyze model decisions, but it does not test the claim versions about neuron interpretability audits or their alternatives.
record.gate_note: The study reports a zero-ablation experiment on three SAE neurons and downstream driving scores (Table II). These results concern SAE features in autonomous-driving models, not the neuron interpretability shares or tests specified in V1–V7, so the rows are recorded with versions ["none"]. Other reported SAE reconstruction and probing metrics do not measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study trains SAEs on a driving model's latent space and assumes raw neurons are polysemantic. It reports SAE quality metrics and the effect of ablating three SAE features on driving scores. It never measures what share of raw or SAE neurons have one main job, does not compare tools or architectures on interpretability share, and does not score explanations. None of V1–V7 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is correct. The authors conclude that SAE concept analysis exposes spurious learned correlations in end-to-end driving models. They find that ablating three selected SAE features at inference improves EPDMS beyond the original model, with safer trajectories and less ego progress. They add that fully understanding the concepts remains open.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies SAEs to latent representations in autonomous-driving models and intervenes on SAE feature activations; it does not conduct the cited neuron-pole audit or evaluate the claim's explanation tests.

fits_no_version.finding: In GTRS, zero-ablating SAE features 177, 59 and 71 raised EPDMS from 0.4963 to 0.5926 and improved most subscores. Ego progress fell from 0.6378 to 0.5378.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ablating selected SAE features can correct driving-model behaviour at inference time, trading progress for safety and compliance.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors say SAEs do not guarantee every neuron maps to a well-defined concept, so an exhaustive dictionary is not feasible. No share is given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In driving-model SAEs, not all features are interpretable (qualitative only).

record.problems: The reported intervention ablates a selected set of three SAE neurons; uncertainty estimates are not reported for the Table II scores. The study does not quantify how many neurons have identifiable semantics.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version results were available to extract. SAE parametrization and reconstruction/probing metrics in Table I, and qualitative concept examples elsewhere, do not measure the claim versions.

untested.parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or job shares.
No interpretability shares across language models, MoE models or scale.
No reanalysis of canonical polysemantic neurons such as InceptionV1's cat-and-car neuron.
No measured share of interpretable neurons by architecture or tool. The paper states raw neurons are polysemantic but only asserts this, with no measurement.
Circuits are built on SAE features, not the model's own neurons. No comparison of the two.
Explanations from activating examples are not tested for predicting where neurons fire. The text notes some SAE neurons lack clear semantics but gives no number.

record.verdict_notes: Applied paper on autonomous driving. It adopts the superposition and polysemanticity framing that the essay disputes, but provides no evidence on neuron interpretability shares. Table I's SAE metrics (reconstruction, ego correlation, probing) also do not bear on any version. The ablated neurons were selected by the authors and no uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or their job counts.
No comparison of neuron interpretability shares across language models, model sizes, or dense and mixture-of-experts architectures.
No analysis of InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons or recursive generalization.
No comparison of interpretability shares across architectures or tools, and no InceptionV1-sized vision-model estimates.
No test of attribution graphs built from a large model's own neurons or of their explanatory sufficiency and reconstruction error.
No test of explanations against held-out activation examples or firing predictions.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.
